topic: Local-minimax certified sharp inference for hidden-recanting-witness mediation under incomplete proxies: in the fixed finite Wu–Bai–Cui proxy-augmented SCM with a three-state hidden recanting witness and binary proxy channels of rank at most two, define the compact one-SCM sharp set for E[Y(M2(M1(0),1),M1(0),0)] and its two-law Hellinger local modulus Omega_P(r); construct terminating NPM-CERT response-function polynomial programs for sharp endpoints and Omega with feasible SCM witnesses and branch-and-bound/SOS outer certificates, invert simultaneous multinomial confidence fibers for uniform whole-set coverage, prove matching local-minimax upper and lower excess-enlargement bounds governed by Omega_P(n^(-1/2)), and recover root-n enlargement only under an explicit Robinson metric-regularity condition; include the positive rank-two three-state witness and the NLSY97 high-school-track-to-wage consumer

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the compact one-SCM sharp identified set for E[Y(M2(M1(0),1),M1(0),0)] in the finite Wu–Bai–Cui graph when M1 has three states and both binary proxy channels have rank at most two.

source_refs.claim: The paper defines this nested mean, emphasizes that both occurrences of M1(0) are the same individual-level realization, and identifies it under complete bridge conditions.
source_refs.author: Sihan Wu, Yang Bai, Yifan Cui

source_refs.claim: Incomplete proxies can yield causal bounds without identifying a bridge, including analogous hidden-mediator results, but the hidden-recanting shared-witness target is not characterized.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Finite discrete SCM bounding problems admit exact response-function polynomial representations, including incomplete and mismeasured data.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: construct a positive-cell observed law P^rw ... after the three conditional proxy routes ... fail completeness

open_problems.why_unsolved: Wu–Bai–Cui's bridge argument requires completeness, which fails dimensionally when a three-state witness is measured only through binary rank-two channels. The nested target cannot be bounded by independently varying two bridge solutions because the same latent response M1(0) feeds both M2 and Y. The closest prior CausalSmith recanting angle was rejected because its response masses were not bound to the declared SCM fiber and its no-proxy comparator was undefined. The first missing step is therefore an exact two-way correspondence between one common response-function SCM and the polynomial fiber; this is an SCM identification problem with a partial-identification secondary axis.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality between the query image over the fixed compatible-SCM class and a nonempty compact semialgebraic set Θ(P), with attained algebraic endpoints and explicit compatible SCM witnesses attaining both endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact hidden-recanting graph, nested target, proxy assumptions, and NLSY97 tracking-to-wage motivation whose completeness boundary is being replaced by a sharp set.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Path-specific wage mechanisms matter -> a hidden recanting witness defeats ordinary mediation identification -> complete proxies recover the target -> incomplete binary proxies require the exact residual causal set.

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize finite latent variables into deterministic response types, encode observed-law compatibility polynomially, and prove sharpness by constructing SCMs from feasible optimizer masses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired set is a finite discrete-SCM query image, but its proof must additionally preserve the shared M1(0) response and proxy-factorization constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace completeness-based inversion by optimization over proxy-compatible latent completions without requiring a unique bridge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest incomplete-proxy partial-identification argument, while the new target needs one shared recanting-witness SCM.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive an efficient influence function from complete bridge equations and obtain cross-fitted proximal multiply robust root-n inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the inference benchmark that a sharp-set procedure should recover on regular singleton submodels.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the local-minimax excess-enlargement rate for confidence sets of the rank-deficient hidden-recanting sharp set through its two-law Hellinger modulus, and characterize when root-n enlargement follows from Robinson metric regularity.

source_refs.claim: For functional estimation, the Hellinger modulus at radius n^(-1/2) controls minimax risk up to constants in broad convex models.
source_refs.author: David L. Donoho, Richard C. Liu

source_refs.claim: Dualized Le Cam theory gives conditions under which hardest two-point alternatives and bias-variance optimization yield matching minimax bounds for functional estimation.
source_refs.author: Yury Polyanskiy, Yihong Wu

source_refs.claim: Robinson derives error bounds controlling displacement of feasible and optimal solution sets under perturbations of nonlinear programs.
source_refs.author: Stephen M. Robinson

source_refs.claim: Root-n asymptotic normality is established only in the point-identified model with unique bridge solutions, operator surjectivity, and nuisance-rate conditions.
source_refs.author: Sihan Wu, Yang Bai, Yifan Cui

source_refs.excerpt: exact normalizations and weak limits ... at regular pairs, active-entropy pairs, and support-changing contact pairs
Same-class minimax corollaries give root-n quotient-law risk ... using factorization-preserving paths
The core does not claim unrestricted-cardinality sharpness, point identification, inference

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parameter is a set-valued optimum map of a nonconvex polynomial SCM fiber, not the smooth scalar functional handled by Wu–Bai–Cui or the linear convex functionals in classical modulus theory. Rank loss, optimizer-face switches, and merging feasible branches can make endpoint displacement Hölder rather than Lipschitz. The prior recanting proposal stopped before inference, the common-entropy analogue left its regular-versus-contact Hausdorff law open, and the proxy-effect-law run obtained a Lipschitz rate only for a single-valued quotient law. The missing first step is a coderivative or error-bound analysis of the semialgebraic feasible correspondence that also supports factorization-preserving Hellinger submodels.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem defining Ω_P(r) as the worst local Hausdorff displacement over compatible two-law Hellinger pairs, proving matching upper and two-point lower excess-enlargement bounds of order Ω_P(n^(-1/2)), and giving a sharp Robinson metric-regularity condition for Ω_P(r)=O(r) with slower singular counterexamples.

writing_exemplar.why: It fixes the destination graph and regular root-n benchmark, making the loss of bridge uniqueness and operator regularity under incomplete proxies visible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hidden recanting witnesses require proxy inversion -> complete regular operators permit efficient root-n inference -> rank-deficient proxies produce a nonsmooth set-valued target -> a local Hellinger modulus determines attainable enlargement.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate minimax risk to a Hellinger modulus and reduce the converse to hardest nearby two-law tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested Ω_P is the set-valued analogue intended to govern the same n^(-1/2) indistinguishability scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a modulus of continuity to construct honest rate-optimal confidence procedures and matching testing lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the closest procedure-plus-converse template for excess enlargement governed by Ω_P.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert constraint-residual perturbations into controlled displacement of feasible and optimal solution sets through a nonlinear-program error bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Applied to the response-function fiber, this is the first step from root-n multinomial-law error to root-n sharp-set enlargement.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a terminating certified solver for both sharp endpoints and the two-law Hellinger local modulus of the rank-deficient hidden-recanting sharp-set map, returning primal SCM witnesses and checkable branch-and-bound or SOS outer certificates.

source_refs.claim: Autobounds reduces discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs and refines valid outer ranges through dual relaxation and spatial branch-and-bound with epsilon-sharpness guarantees.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Polynomial optimization on compact semialgebraic sets admits a convergent hierarchy of moment and sum-of-squares outer relaxations.
source_refs.author: Jean B. Lasserre

source_refs.claim: Finite convergence of the Lasserre hierarchy follows under constraint qualification, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency, and holds generically under an Archimedean condition.
source_refs.author: Jiawang Nie

source_refs.excerpt: nested inner and outer complexes converge in Hausdorff distance ... including boxes whose witness has a zero latent mass
State an explicit input encoding and worst-case complexity/output-size bound for CAD_m and CAD_conf.
The supporting finite response-function program is nonconvex polynomial optimization.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Autobounds does not specialize the proxy conditional-independence equations, channel-rank minors, shared hidden-witness responses, and a second compatible observed law constrained by Hellinger distance into one certificate-producing program. The Hellinger square root also needs an algebraic lift. Prior CausalSmith work supplied only a nonconvex program handle; analogous certification proposals left termination open at zero latent masses, active constraints, and singular boxes. The first changed proof step is to replace ordinary response-function subdivision by boxes carrying proxy-rank minors, nested-response compatibility, and coupled two-law constraints, where regular interval-Newton tests alone cannot certify exclusion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-input NPM-CERT theorem proving epsilon-termination and soundness for endpoint and Ω_P(r) programs, with feasible one- or two-law SCM witnesses for inner bounds, certified outer bounds, and a computable stopping gap converging to zero.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames certified computation as the bridge between an abstract partial-identification query and a usable guaranteed answer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Analytic sharp bounds are often intractable -> finite SCMs yield polynomial programs -> global relaxations provide certified causal ranges -> extend certification to hidden-recanting endpoints and their Hellinger modulus.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine response-function canonicalization with dual relaxations and spatial branch-and-bound so every intermediate outer range remains causally valid.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its first changed step is construction of a coupled two-law feasible set with rank-minor, shared-response, and Hellinger-lift constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace polynomial positivity on a compact semialgebraic feasible set by moment matrices and SOS localizing certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides independently checkable outer certificates for both endpoint and modulus programs.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact multinomial tests and optimize a target function over accepted probability vectors to retain finite-sample coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The solver must propagate every accepted observed law through the nonlinear SCM fiber while preserving the coverage certificate.

open_problems.open_problem: Obtain simultaneous confidence-fiber inference with uniform whole-set coverage for the hidden-recanting sharp set under finite multinomial sampling, including simplex faces and laws where optimizer branches merge.

source_refs.claim: The paper leaves formal inference for its mediation bounds open and warns that the standard bootstrap is inconsistent near parameter-space boundaries.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Arvid Sjölander, Dean Follmann, Michael C. Sachs

source_refs.claim: The authors construct random sets that contain the entire identified set and give conditions for uniform coverage over classes of observed-data laws.
source_refs.author: Joseph P. Romano, Azeem M. Shaikh

source_refs.claim: Exact test inversion gives finite-sample confidence intervals for arbitrary real functions of k-sample multinomial probabilities, including boundary and nonsmooth cases.
source_refs.author: Michael C. Sachs, Erin E. Gabriel, Michael P. Fay

source_refs.claim: Calibrated projection yields uniformly valid inference for projections of partially identified parameters by optimizing over relaxed sample moment constraints.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, Jörg Stoye

open_problems.why_unsolved: The endpoints are nonsmooth optimized functions of many multinomial cells, and rank deficiency creates singular laws where active polynomial branches change. Wu–Bai–Cui's influence-function interval presumes unique complete bridges, while the closest mediation-bounds paper expressly leaves boundary-robust inference unresolved. General set-inference and exact-multinomial results do not establish that taking the union of certified causal sharp sets over one simultaneous observed-law confidence fiber covers the entire hidden-recanting set uniformly. This is an estimation-and-inference contribution, distinct from identifying Θ(P).
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous multinomial confidence fiber C_n and a computable union of certified Θ(Q) over Q in C_n, together with a finite-sample or uniform asymptotic theorem that this random set contains all of Θ(P) with probability at least 1-alpha over the fixed finite SCM class.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly distinguishes inference on one admissible point from simultaneous coverage of an identified set.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Partial identification produces a population set -> sampling uncertainty perturbs that set -> separate endpoint intervals need not cover it simultaneously -> invert a common law-level test to obtain uniform whole-set coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact multinomial tests and optimize over accepted probability vectors to guarantee finite-sample coverage at boundaries and nonsmooth targets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The observed law is a collection of multinomial vectors; the new argument lifts their simultaneous accepted fiber through a set-valued causal map.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate whole-set coverage into familywise control of an indexed collection of null hypotheses and establish uniform validity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested guarantee is containment of every value in Θ(P), not coverage of a selected causal value.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate relaxed sample constraints and repeatedly solve global projection problems to cover a target functional uniformly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest optimization-aware inference argument, but the destination requires a nonconvex polynomial SCM fiber and whole-set coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when the Wu–Bai–Cui nested path-specific mean remains point identified with a three-state hidden recanting witness and two binary proxy channels of rank at most two, rather than equating failure of completeness with target nonidentification.

source_refs.claim: Its three point-identification strategies require proxy completeness; for discrete models the stated sufficient dimension condition fails with binary proxies and a three-state witness.
source_refs.author: Sihan Wu, Yang Bai, Yifan Cui

source_refs.claim: Completeness is untestable and incomplete proxies can still partially identify causal targets without identifying a bridge, but no target-specific singleton frontier is given for hidden recanting mediation.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Finite proxy identification uses matrix rank and completeness to make latent inversion unique, supplying a sufficient route rather than a target-specific necessity result.
source_refs.author: Wang Miao, Zhi Geng, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Each binary proxy operator has a nontrivial kernel when the witness has three states, so the bridge-uniqueness proof cannot apply. That failure does not imply that this scalar nested mean varies along every observationally invisible direction: target-specific cancellations can make Θ(P) a singleton at exceptional or structured laws. Existing work supplies completeness-based sufficient conditions and partial bounds for simpler proxy targets, but not a necessary-and-sufficient algebraic frontier for this shared-witness counterfactual.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient finite algebraic criterion for Θ(P) to be a singleton, paired with observationally equivalent SCM counterexamples off the criterion and an explicit positive rank-two three-state SCM satisfying it.

writing_exemplar.why: It poses the exact hidden-recanting problem and makes completeness the boundary that the new target-specific criterion would sharpen.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Recanting witnesses invalidate ordinary mediation -> complete proxies identify the target -> binary proxies cannot be complete for a three-state witness -> determine exactly when the target nevertheless remains unique.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate proxy completeness into finite conditional-probability matrix rank and use the resulting inverse-system argument to identify latent quantities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired frontier is the target-specific rank-deficient counterpart of this finite-proxy identification argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize the causal functional over proxy-compatible latent completions instead of requiring a uniquely identified bridge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how to separate failure of bridge uniqueness from failure of target identification.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bridge-based efficient influence functions and cross-fitted multiply robust estimation under unique solvability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the natural limit theory to recover on regular singleton strata of the new algebraic frontier.

open_problems.open_problem: Exhibit a rational positive-cell rank-two three-state hidden-recanting SCM whose incomplete proxies strictly exclude a no-proxy endpoint for E[Y(M2(M1(0),1),M1(0),0)], and extend it to an observable open-class strict-contraction criterion.

source_refs.excerpt: Supply a fully rational worked P^dagger with nonzero cells and a machine-checkable endpoint-face certificate
Strengthen ... to an observable sufficient criterion for strict contraction over a named open class
construct a positive-cell observed law P^rw ... after the three conditional proxy routes ... fail completeness

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior run delegated the recanting target and never produced a nonvacuous witness; its contraction construction concerned only simple mediation. For this target one must define the no-proxy endpoint face on the same nested response family and prove that rank-two proxy factorization excludes that face without using zero cells or silently restoring completeness. Extending one example to an open class additionally requires an observable quantitative separation margin that survives perturbations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully rational positive-cell SCM and observed law with proxy operators of rank exactly two, an explicit strict endpoint inequality against the matching no-proxy set, a checkable endpoint-face infeasibility certificate, and an observable margin preserving the inequality on a neighborhood.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the hidden-recanting scientific setup and the NLSY97 path-specific wage target for which a nonvacuous incomplete-proxy witness matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hidden recanting obstructs ordinary mediation identification -> complete proxies restore a point formula -> realistic binary proxies may be incomplete -> a positive rank-two witness must show that they can still shrink the causal set.

method_exemplars.technique: Search a finite response-function polynomial program for a primal model and certify endpoint exclusion through a global dual bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired exhibit pairs a concrete finite SCM witness with a certificate that the competing no-proxy endpoint is unattainable.

method_exemplars.technique: Use incomplete proxy restrictions to derive informative causal bounds without bridge uniqueness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It establishes the phenomenon to be witnessed, while the new construction must preserve the recanting cross-world coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the path-specific target with proximal bridge moments and root-n inference under complete-proxy regularity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The rank-two witness should mark the boundary between this regular point-identified regime and informative partial identification.

literature_map:
Avin–Shpitser–Pearl (2005, IJCAI) introduced the recanting-witness obstruction for path-specific effects.
Shpitser (2013, Cognitive Science) generalized the obstruction to recanting districts under hidden-variable longitudinal mediation.
Shpitser–Tchetgen Tchetgen (2016, Annals of Statistics) organized node, edge, and path interventions through the edge g-formula.
Gabriel–Sjölander–Follmann–Sachs (2023, Biostatistics) derived tight binary cross-direct-effect bounds but left formal bound inference, multilevel variables, and intermediate confounders open.
Miao–Geng–Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018, Biometrika) made proxy rank/completeness the finite-model route to unique proximal identification.
Dukes–Shpitser–Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, Biometrika) developed proximal mediation with efficient, multiply robust inference under latent confounding.
Wu–Bai–Cui (2026, arXiv:2606.17600) is the exact anchor: it defines the nested mean, gives three complete-bridge identification routes and efficient inference, and uses NLSY97 high-school tracking and wages.
Ghassami–Shpitser–Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, arXiv:2304.04374) shows incomplete proxies can sharpen bounds without completeness, but treats simpler causal-effect and hidden-mediator targets.
Duarte–Finkelstein–Knox–Mummolo–Shpitser (2024, JASA) supplies exact response-function polynomial representations, spatial branch-and-bound, and epsilon-sharp causal certificates.
Lasserre (2001, SIAM Journal on Optimization) and Nie (2014, Mathematical Programming) provide SOS/moment outer certificates and finite-convergence conditions.
Chernozhukov–Hong–Tamer (2007), Romano–Shaikh (2010), and Kaido–Molinari–Stoye (2019), all Econometrica, separate set estimation, whole-set coverage, and calibrated projection.
Sachs–Gabriel–Fay (2024, arXiv:2406.19141) gives exact inversion for arbitrary functions of multinomial probabilities, a natural source for simultaneous law fibers.
Donoho–Liu (1991, Annals of Statistics) and Polyanskiy–Wu (2026, Annals of Statistics) connect Hellinger moduli and hardest two-law alternatives to matching minimax rates.
Robinson (1973, Mathematical Programming) supplies the error-bound mechanism separating Lipschitz root-n laws from singular rank-deficient laws.
Targeted searches found no paper combining incomplete proxies for a hidden recanting witness with one-SCM sharpness, certified two-law Hellinger-modulus computation, and matching local-minimax whole-set inference.
prior_proposal_map:
The target qid contained only state and orchestration records, with no prior proposal or review for this exact run.
The bounded catalogue scan prioritized proxy, mediation, recanting, certification, confidence-fiber, and modulus qids across active and banked runs.
Failed scm_prox_recant_pid_v1 was deep-mined, including its three rejected proto cores and angle3 reviewer; its recanting branch remained undefined at the compatible-SCM/program interface.
Legacy pid_mediation_proxy_v1 and its rejected angle were inspected; its bridge-null sharpness conjecture was refuted, so that outer set was not reused as a sharp SCM fiber.
Downgraded pid_commonentropy_benefit_harm_contact_v1 supplied singular-certification and regular-versus-contact Hausdorff-inference questions, including zero-mass strata.
Downgraded scm_finiteplate_bernstein_ate_bounds_v1 supplied the reviewer demand for encoded termination and output-size guarantees for exact polynomial recovery.
Active stat_proxy_effectlaw_eigencollision_frontier_v1 supplied a modulus-to-upper/lower-risk architecture and factorization-preserving local paths.
Downgraded scm_fortified_proxy_threshold_v1 was inspected as a rank-feasibility warning: row counting is insufficient without a compatible positive-minor witness.
No prior entry combines the exact hidden-recanting target, incomplete rank-two proxies, certified sharp-set computation, and local-minimax set enlargement.
